[[Category:Logic fallacy]]
'''Correlation-causation fallacy''' is the mistaken [[belief]] that correlation implies causation.

== Examples ==

[[File:Baby vaccination.png|thumbnail|Vaccination schedule and typical diagnostic timeline for autism overlap: they are statistically correlated. But it does not mean one causes another. Concluding vaccination causes autism from a simple correlation is no less absurd than concluding autism causes vaccination.]]
* Numerous children were diagnosed with [[autism spectrum disorder (ASD)]] shortly after receiving vaccinations $\Rightarrow $ [[Vaccination]] causes autism<ref>{{#cite:Q2910}}</ref>
